choices.text: Recommend East Market Hotel: $228 per night, 4.6 guest rating, breakfast available for $13 per day, a 5-minute walk to the workshop, and a restaurant across the street open until 10:30 p.m.
Recommend Central Arcade Hotel: $241 per night, 4.4 guest rating, breakfast included, a 7-minute walk to the workshop, and an on-site restaurant open until 11:00 p.m.
Recommend Union Station Inn: $233 per night, 4.5 guest rating, breakfast available for $9 per day, a 6-minute walk to the workshop, and a lobby bistro open until 9:00 p.m.
Recommend Lafayette Square Hotel: $238 per night, 4.7 guest rating, breakfast included, a 12-minute walk to the workshop, and a restaurant on the same block open until 11:00 p.m.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: no option dominates on ordinary attributes. A offers the strongest rating and shortest walk, B offers confirmed inclusion and on-site late dining at the same breakfast-adjusted cost, C is slightly more expensive after breakfast but closer and better rated than B, and D is cheaper and highly rated but farther away. Selecting B requires applying the early-work-stay breakfast preference as a soft tie-breaker alongside dining access.
probes.gold_action: Recommend Central Arcade Hotel first, with East Market Hotel as the close alternative. Over the three workshop mornings, East Market's $228 rate plus $13 breakfast equals Central Arcade's $241 included-breakfast rate. Since both ratings exceed Maya's normal quality floor and both walks are practical, the confirmed included breakfast and later on-site dinner make Central Arcade the better balanced lead rather than treating breakfast as an absolute rule.
probes.label_rationale: The evidence makes free breakfast a recurring but soft preference, especially for early work mornings: breakfast may matter more before 9:00 a.m. meetings (s0002), is useful for 8:00 a.m. sessions (s0064), but is not a dealbreaker and should be confirmed rather than assumed (s0015). B does not impose a material location or quality sacrifice relative to A: the breakfast-adjusted cost is equal, the walk difference is two minutes, and B adds later on-site dining. A remains a genuine alternative because it has the better rating and shorter walk; D remains viable because of its lower rate and higher rating but gives up five minutes of walking convenience each way.
probes.query: Maya needs a Tuesday-to-Friday hotel in St. Louis for a planning workshop. Sessions begin at 8:00 a.m. each morning, and she will not rent a car. All options are refundable, within policy, have the same room type, and meet the 4.0 guest-rating floor on the same site. Which recommendation should lead?

choices.text: Hold King Street Hotel first: $305 per night, 4.6 guest rating, breakfast available for $16 per family per day, a 4-minute walk to the museum, and a restaurant across the street.
Hold Meeting Street Suites first: $321 per night, 4.4 guest rating, breakfast included, a 6-minute walk to the museum, and an all-day cafe on site.
Hold Wharf House first: $311 per night, 4.5 guest rating, breakfast available for $11 per family per day, a 5-minute walk to the museum, and a restaurant one block away.
Hold Harbor Square Hotel first: $316 per night, 4.7 guest rating, breakfast included, an 11-minute walk to the museum, and an on-site restaurant.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: the choices deliberately create cross-cutting tradeoffs rather than a generic winner. A and B have the same effective daily cost if the family uses hotel breakfast, but A has better rating and proximity while B has inclusion and on-site food. C is nearly tied on effective cost with a better rating and shorter walk than B, while D combines inclusion, price, and rating but is substantially farther for the timed museum morning. The history is needed to give modest weight to included breakfast without allowing it to defeat practical centrality.
probes.gold_action: Hold Meeting Street Suites first, with King Street Hotel as the close alternative. King Street's $305 rate plus the $16 family breakfast equals Meeting Street's $321 included-breakfast rate. Meeting Street remains centrally practical for the timed museum entry, and its included breakfast plus on-site cafe are useful for a no-car family weekend without making breakfast override location.
probes.label_rationale: For family travel, the evidence says breakfast helps with a child but is not a hard rule (s0004). It also firmly limits the preference: Maya would not accept a poor location merely for free breakfast (s0034) and does not want breakfast savings to push the family too far out (s0048). B satisfies that boundary: its six-minute walk is still very convenient, its three-night breakfast-adjusted cost matches A, and it adds an on-site cafe. A is a credible close alternative because it is two minutes closer and slightly better rated; D has stronger rating and a lower room rate but gives up meaningful no-car walking convenience; C offers a middle position on price, rating, and distance.
probes.query: Maya is deciding which cancellable Friday-to-Monday Charleston hotel hold should lead for two adults and one child. They will not have a car, have a 10:00 a.m. timed museum entry on Saturday, and need two queens. Every option is refundable, within policy, and meets the requested 4.0 guest-rating floor on the same site. Breakfast charges are confirmed total daily charges for the family. Which hold should lead?

choices.text: Recommend River Market Hotel: $220 per night, 4.7 guest rating, a $10 daily cafe credit that may be used at breakfast but is not listed as breakfast included, a 5-minute walk to the client site, and on-site dining until 10:00 p.m.
Recommend Union Square Hotel: $230 per night, 4.5 guest rating, continental breakfast included, a 7-minute walk to the client site, and an on-site restaurant open until 11:00 p.m.
Recommend Park Avenue Hotel: $224 per night, 4.6 guest rating, breakfast available for $7 per day, a 6-minute walk to the client site, and a lobby bistro open until 9:30 p.m.
Recommend Old Depot Hotel: $222 per night, 4.8 guest rating, breakfast included, a 14-minute walk to the client site with two major street crossings, and an on-site restaurant open until 11:00 p.m.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: A, B, C, and D each present a plausible but incompatible bundle of rating, price, breakfast certainty, late-arrival dining, and walking convenience. Query-only reasoning cannot determine whether a cafe credit should be valued like confirmed breakfast, whether a continental breakfast is sufficient, or how much weight to assign a seven-minute versus fourteen-minute no-car morning walk. The correct action depends on Maya's specific preference to verify unlisted breakfast, prefer inclusion when otherwise comparable, and avoid sacrificing hotel access solely for breakfast.
probes.gold_action: Recommend Union Square Hotel first and keep River Market Hotel as the close alternate, but verify River Market's breakfast terms before treating its cafe credit as equivalent to included breakfast. Union Square provides confirmed included breakfast, accepts the ordinary continental offering without inventing a higher breakfast standard, supports the late Sunday arrival with on-site food, and remains much more convenient for the early no-car workshop mornings than Old Depot.
probes.label_rationale: The relevant history requires two linked judgments. Maya does not want breakfast assumed to be included when it is not clearly stated (s0015), and included breakfast is particularly useful before 8:00 a.m. sessions (s0064). At the same time, hotel access can be worth accepting paid breakfast, so breakfast should not justify an inconvenient hotel (s0105). B respects both sides: it has explicitly included breakfast and late on-site food while staying seven minutes from the site. A is attractive on rating and location, but a cafe credit is not the same verified service and should be checked rather than assumed equivalent. D has included breakfast and a strong rating but its 14-minute, crossing-heavy walk is a meaningful convenience drawback for the early no-car workdays. Nothing in the history requires a full breakfast, so B's continental offering is sufficient evidence of inclusion.
probes.query: Maya needs a Sunday-to-Thursday Omaha hotel for a four-night client workshop. Her first sessions begin at 8:15 a.m., she will not rent a car, and her Sunday flight reaches the hotel area around 9:30 p.m. All offers are refundable, within policy, have the same room type, and meet the 4.0 guest-rating floor on the same site. Which recommendation should lead?
